From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-side review of Seller's SPA positions and Disclosure Letter

**Threshold points**
- **Treat every item as open.** The "[STANDARD]" tags, the "FINAL / settled at principal level" statement and the "no further scrutiny" note are the Seller's assertions. Nothing in the package shows Wattlebridge agreed them. Please confirm with the deal team whether any principal-level agreement exists. Until then I have reviewed everything.
- **The Seller's market claims are unverified.** Its "market" ranges are one-sided and untested.
- **Limits of this review.** I have only the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter, not the full SPA draft or the DD-002 to DD-012 documents. Clause references are as the Seller describes them.
- **Figures are indicative.** The counter-proposals below are negotiating positions to be confirmed by the deal team, not settled market benchmarks.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer should want:** A higher general cap, with title/fundamental, tax, specific indemnities and fraud outside it (capped at price or uncapped as appropriate).
- **Recommendation:** Counter at about 30–35% (AUD 7.2–8.4m), with 25% as a fallback only if the specific indemnities and separate tiers are secured. The cap is tolerable only if the known risks (Bluefen, data incident, Ironquay IP) sit outside it.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket (about 1.04% of price), with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** A lower de minimis with aggregation of related claims, and a tipping (first-dollar) basket.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at AUD 10,000 de minimis and a tipping basket of about 0.5% (about AUD 120,000). The thresholds should not apply to fundamental, tax, IP/data or indemnity claims. A deductible basket plus a high de minimis erodes recoveries on a business this size.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months, and any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated.
- **Buyer should want:** At least 24 months, covering two audit cycles. Longer periods for tax, IP/data and fundamental claims, and no limit for fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "applies to all Claims" language. Counter at 24 months for general claims, with express longer periods for the other categories. Otherwise the 18-month limit swallows the title, tax and fraud claims.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, solvency) capped at the full price, with no thresholds and a long limitation period (6 years or more).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. A title failure goes to the root of what the Buyer is paying AUD 24m for, so a 20% cap is unacceptable.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** None. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out so that caps, thresholds, time limits, the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses, and disclosure do not apply to fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation or wilful concealment.
- **Recommendation:** Insist on it. As drafted, the Seller could be shielded from the consequences of its own fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (as at 5pm 22 Sept 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sch 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer should want:** Specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties only. It should be in sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Generic data-room, register and public-record disclosure should be excluded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. It would let the Seller disclose away most warranties by the volume of the data room. Also fix the disclosure cut-off date (the 22 Sept data room is already six weeks old), with no right to update after signing without Buyer consent.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** No knowledge qualifier, or at most actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals. Constructive or "discoverable" knowledge should be excluded, and the SPA should state that Buyer rights are unaffected by its investigations.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3. Combined with general disclosure it removes warranty protection for anything in the data room. Note also that statutory misleading-conduct exposure may not be fully excludable by contract, but do not rely on that.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The consent is "treated as satisfied" on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter admits no final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions exists (about AUD 3.6m, about 30% of revenue; DD-002 cl 11.2/11.3).
- **Buyer should want:** A condition precedent for an unconditional written consent in agreed form. The cl 11.3 conditions should be satisfied or waived by Bluefen. Only the Buyer should be able to waive it, and there should be a long-stop date with a right to terminate.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's wording. A consent delivered with unmet conditions would "satisfy" the condition without protecting the revenue. Consider also a price adjustment or deferred consideration if Bluefen is waived or delayed.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion" (about AUD 3.2m outstanding). The Disclosure Letter confirms it is not repaid and there is no discharge.
- **Buyer should want:** A payout letter before Completion. Repayment from sale proceeds through the funds flow, with simultaneous release and discharge of all security (including PPSR and any share security), and the change-control clause (8.1) dealt with.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. This is a debt-free/cash-free deal, so the debt must be repaid at Completion out of price. Check whether Riverlark's security extends to the shares, since that also affects title.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 of Completion bonuses (DD-005) are "a matter for the Seller" and not in the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter does not say whether on-costs apply.
- **Buyer should want:** The bonuses and related on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, workers' compensation) treated as Seller transaction costs or debt-like items, paid at Completion through the funds flow or deducted from price.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. They are triggered by the sale and would otherwise fall on the Company post-Completion. Get tax advisers to quantify the on-costs, which could add materially above AUD 420,000. Also require a specific indemnity.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Buyer should want:** Payment of the AUD 180,000 (DD-010) and a confirmatory assignment of the SOW3 Project Materials as Completion deliverables. The indemnity should be broadened to any Ironquay claim over IP ownership or use, sit outside the general cap and thresholds, and be supported by a retention or escrow if unresolved.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as inadequate. Under DD-004 cl 7.3 the IP does not transfer until every SOW3 fee has cleared. The real exposure is ownership of platform code, not just AUD 180,000. The Seller concedes there is no payment receipt or assignment, and DD-010 is not bank verification.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material (cl 4.6 / Sch 6).
- **Buyer should want:** A specific indemnity (uncapped or capped at price) for costs, regulatory action and third-party claims. It should also cover a Seller covenant to complete the investigation and any required notifications, delivery of the final report before Completion, and a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the characterisation. The Disclosure Letter admits access, scope and notification obligations are unknown, with about 1,240 records involved and no loss figure. Ask whether a Privacy Act notifiable-data-breach assessment was completed, since the 30-day assessment period has probably run from the 22 Sept data. Obtain all correspondence and forensic material.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** Facts on whether each renewal is committed, terminable, accrued or paid, and why three AUD 110,000 renewals are structured separately. Buyer consent should be required for renewals and commitments before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label until the facts are known (the Disclosure Letter does not support it). If the amounts are committed or prepaid, treat them as debt-like or working-capital items, and add interim-period covenants.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** One regime for all Claims. Clauses 12.3 and 13 apply "to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise", and 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer should want:** Separate tiers, each with its own cap, thresholds and time limit: general warranties; fundamental/title; tax; IP and data; specific indemnities; and fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the single-regime approach. It is the mechanism by which the cap, thresholds and time limits reach everything else.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012, which the Disclosure Letter says is only the source relied on and not Buyer-verified.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification: ASIC extracts, transfer and issue history, Seller authority and board approvals, and confirmation of no options, rights or encumbrances (including under Riverlark security). The Seller should also deliver share transfers, certificates and a title warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register. Complete verification before signing and make the deliverables a Completion requirement. Title is only as good as the Company's own records until verified.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer should want:** A pre-Completion tax indemnity (not subject to the basket or de minimis), a longer claims period (about 5 years, or the ATO amendment period plus a buffer), and strong IP ownership, open-source and contractor-assignment warranties outside the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled". Nothing in the package shows agreement, and the general regime (20% cap, 18 months) is inadequate for a SaaS business whose value is its IP and customer data.

---

**Suggested next steps**
1. Confirm with the deal team that none of these positions was agreed at principal level.
2. Send a mark-up that rejects the Seller's single-regime structure and the [STANDARD] framing.
3. Issue a follow-up DD request list covering Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the incident, Sandbar and title.
4. Settle a list of Completion deliverables and conditions (Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout letter and discharge, Ironquay payment and assignment, bonuses in the funds flow).
5. Price protection: consider a retention or escrow sized to the open items (Ironquay, the incident and Bluefen) if they are not resolved before signing.
